scope: KP_SIGNIFICATOR_V1: a single narrow judgment - does the 7th house cusp's KP cuspal sub-lord signify the marriage-promise house group (2,7,11) or the marriage-denial group (1,6,10,12) - for a natal chart under the KP_KRISHNAMURTI profile. PRODUCTION implementation: engine.kp.significators, discoverable via engine.kp.significators.judge_marriage(chart).

rule.significator_strength_order: star-of-occupant > occupant > star-of-owner > owner (union test for V1's own binary judgment, ADR-0078 section 4)
rule.aspect_convention: same-sign conjunction (no orb); universal 7th aspect for every planet, plus Mars 4th/8th, Jupiter 5th/9th, Saturn 3rd/10th (ADR-0078 section 3, KP-scoped, independently implemented)
rule.node_substitution_priority: conjoined planet > aspecting planet > sign lord fallback (ADR-0078 section 6)
rule.retrograde_rule: conditional-on-direct-motion disclosure qualifier, not a pass/fail gate (ADR-0078 section 5)

oracle.note: no third-party computational oracle exists for KP significators (DP-028 section D, DP-029 section 4); certification rests on cross-implementation agreement between engine.kp.significators (production) and validate_kp_significator_holdout.py (an independently authored, from-scratch reimplementation) - gate I compares production against STATIC values frozen from the independent reimplementation's own output, and gate C runs that reimplementation's own battery standalone. This is agreement between two independently-written implementations of the same frozen rule, not external oracle validation, and is not evidence that the frozen rule itself matches primary KP doctrine (see docs/decisions/DP-030 section 4 for that separate, still-open question).

certification_integrity_repair.defect_found: an external forensic mutation experiment (2026-08-26) proved every gate in the prior version of this file reported PASS while the production module's computed sub-lord was wrong at 3600/3600 sampled longitudes; gate I's own 'independent' reference imported and called engine.kp.significators.signification_set() directly (x == x); the HOLDOUT list carried no expected values of any kind; gates B/E compared kp_chain() against itself and were presented as correctness evidence rather than wiring checks
certification_integrity_repair.repair_summary: gate I rewritten to compare production against STATIC expected values frozen from validate_kp_significator_holdout.py's own from-scratch logic; gates B/E honestly reclassified as wiring/coverage checks (see their own 'classification'/'disclosure' fields); scripts/check_mutation_detection.py extended with a hermetic gate that corrupts engine.kp.significators._signifies() directly and requires detection

B_dense_sweep.scope: 7th cusp longitude sweep, production wiring vs. a second call to the same kp_chain() function used internally by chart construction
B_dense_sweep.disclosure: both sides call the identical kp_chain() function; this proves the production module correctly WIRES that function's output into its own chart data structures across a dense sample, not that kp_chain()'s own values are correct (KP_CHAIN_V1 already certifies that separately against PyJHora) or that the significator-derivation logic downstream is correct (see gate I for that evidence). A prior version of this gate was presented as correctness evidence; corrected 2026-08-27 per the certification-integrity repair, see docs/decisions/DP-030.

C_independent_validator.note: separate-process reimplementation; since 2026-08-27 also checked against static expected data (see validate_kp_significator_holdout.py)

E_boundary_cases.convention: inherited KP_CHAIN_V1 sub-interval boundary set, tested at the 7th cusp
E_boundary_cases.disclosure: the sub-lord portion of this gate calls the same kp_chain() function on both sides (see gate B's own disclosure); only the sign_of() boundary sweep is a genuine second, differently-implemented computation. A prior version of this gate was presented as correctness evidence; corrected 2026-08-27, see docs/decisions/DP-030.

H_strength_order_cases.note: confirms Ordering A's categories are independently recognized; V1's own promise/deny judgment is a union test over the categories, not a priority selection - see ADR-0078 section 4

I_protected_holdout.methodology: production output compared against STATIC expected values frozen from validate_kp_significator_holdout.py's own from-scratch reimplementation (never regenerated by production code at certification time); real ephemeris-driven charts, independent of every deliberately-constructed synthetic case in gates E-H, never used to tune any rule

explicit_non_claims: Four Step Theory (Gondhalekar) - out of scope (ADR-0027 Decision 3)
Ruling Planets - out of scope, horary/judgment-time construct (ADR-0027 Decision 3)
horary/Prashna judgment generally - out of scope
charts with cusps inside the undefined polar-latitude band - unverified (DP-025, still deferred)
the horary-to-natal application of the promise/deny house groups is a disclosed ACE-defined inference, not a direct primary citation for the natal case
the aspect/conjunction convention is a disclosed ACE-defined inference from Krishnamurti's own demonstrated usage, not a single verbatim citation
source text is a scanned/OCR'd reprint, single transcription pass, not a publisher-verified critical edition
the children/5th-house parallel is not covered by V1

no third-party computational oracle corroborates this design - cross-implementation agreement (production vs. an independently-authored reimplementation) is the sole evidentiary basis, disclosed as such and not overstated as oracle validation

Uranus/Neptune/Pluto and the Ascendant are excluded from the candidate occupant/significator pool - not part of the certified KP_LORDS nine-graha cycle and never treated as significators in the retrieved primary text
no interpretation, convergence, BTR, historical prediction, or other KP variant is implemented - engine.kp.significators exposes exactly this one frozen judgment

justified_exceptions: Frozen holdout declarations and oracle imports are permitted only outside engine/; all scanned sources remain subject to suspicious-identifier detection.
